question.leadin: Give the following about lunar exploration.
question.text: Every mission which put people on the moon was part of this NASA program; the 11th, 12th, and 14th through 17th missions of this name were successful at that goal
question.clue: Gene Kranz aborted one of this program's missions, in which an oxygen tank explosion nearly killed James Lovell and his crew.

swap.text: A show on this network called State of the Union is hosted by Jake Tapper. Wolf Blitzer hosts The Situation Room on this Atlanta-based network which pioneered 24/7 news coverage.
swap.clue: In August 2012, an employee here was fired for plagiarism, and his "GPS" show was off the air for a week before he was vindicated. .

question.text: During the term of this president, tensions were heightened when the Soviets shot down an American U2 spy plane. This former World War II general spearheaded the construction of the Interstate Highway system.
question.answerHtml: Dwight D. Eisenhower [or Dwight David Eisenhower or David Dwight Eisenhower or Ike Eisenhower]
question.clue: This politician stated that "it is humanity hanging from a cross of iron" during a speech that listed alternatives to building a heavy bomber.

swap.leadin: Harry Truman visited this city nearly a dozen times as President, establishing a "Little White House."
swap.text: Name this southernmost city of the continental United States. The 2,300-plus miles of U.S. Route 1 run from Fort Kent in Maine south through Miami to this city.
swap.clue: This island was a frequent destination for Harry S. Truman, leading a neighborhood here to be named Truman Annex.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a political scandal in the 80s.
question.text: The Tower Commission investigated this scandal in which American officials used money from secret arms sales to support rebels in Nicaragua.
question.clue: The plan, in violation of the Boland Amendment, was conceived by Robert McFarlane.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Senator Millard E. Tydings, a University of Maryland alumnus and building dedicatee.
swap.text: As the chair of his namesake Tydings Committee, Tydings scrutinized the accusations of this Wisconsin senator, who claimed in a speech given in Wheeling that 205 communists had infiltrated the State Department.
swap.clue: This man's actions with Owen Lattimore involved the creation of the Tydings Committee.

question.leadin: This president's National Commission on Excellence in Education criticized the country's schools in the report A Nation at Risk.
question.text: Name this president whose other children-related policies included the anti-drug "Just Say No" campaign, which was devised by his wife.
question.clue: The Tower Commission investigated this president's cabinet, who had previously violated the Boland Amendment.

swap.leadin: Several rolls of film central to this man's case were purportedly hidden in a pumpkin.
swap.text: Name this State Department official who was accused by Whittaker Chambers of spying for the USSR. As the statute of limitations for espionage had expired by the time of his trial, this man was convicted for perjury instead.
swap.clue: Along with Harry Dexter White, he was implicated by the Moynihan commission using information from the Venona project.

question.text: Brzezinski and Vance both served under this Democratic president, on whose watch the Iran hostage crisis started.
question.clue: This President lost his reelection bid in a race that featured Independent candidate John B. Anderson.

swap.leadin: Identify these British folks who rebelled against Catholic Church doctrine.
swap.text: This group, started by Gerrard Winstanley in 1649, was an offshoot of the Levelers and argued for radical Christian communitarianism and the cultivation of neglected land.
swap.clue: Led early on by William Everard, the philosophy of this group was put forth in The New Law of Righteousness, the primary text by its major leader Gerrard Winstanley.

question.text: This 1962 book by Rachel Carson is credited with kick-starting the environmental movement in the US.
question.clue: This landmark 1962 book by Rachel Carson, credited by many with starting the environmental movement.

swap.leadin: A member of this group, Hale Boggs, later disappeared while flying in Alaska to campaign for one of his colleagues.
swap.text: Name this group, whose findings concluded that the perpetrator of one event was acting alone when he killed police officer J.D. Tippit. This group's findings also introduced the "single-bullet" theory.
swap.clue: John Cooper was joined in this group by the president of the World Bank, John McCloy, while James Lee Rankin served as their General Counsel.

question.leadin: This case introduced a namesake three-pronged "test" for violations of the Establishment Clause in school funding.
question.text: Name this Burger court decision which ruled that a Pennsylvania law allowing for public reimbursement of Catholic school teachers in public schools was unconstitutional.
question.answerHtml: Lemon v. Kurtzman [accept either underlined portion; accept Lemon test]
question.clue: It established a namesake test which requires a "secular legislative purpose" and bars "excessive entanglement with religion." For 15 points, name this 1971 Supreme Court case arising from Pennsylvania's system of tax breaks for parochial schools.

swap.text: All three Apollo 1 crew members previously participated in this second American space program, the successor to Project Mercury. Ed White performed the first American space walk during this program's fourth mission.
swap.clue: Young controversially smuggled a corned beef sandwich on board the first manned mission in this project. Ed White became the first American to complete a spacewalk as part of this successor to the Mercury Project.

question.text: Crabgrass Frontier profiles suburban communities, called this man's namesake "towns," that consisted of plain white houses built them for World War II veterans on Long Island.
question.clue: The techniques used to construct San Lorenzo were later used by this American homebuilder, whose namesake "towns" in Pennsylvania and New York are synonymous with mass-produced postwar housing.

swap.text: This historian ended up on the enemies list after he attacked Nixon in The Imperial Presidency. This former special assistant to JFK glorified the Kennedy presidency in his book A Thousand Days.
swap.answerHtml: Arthur Schlesinger Jr. [do not accept or prompt on “Arthur Schlesinger Sr.”]
swap.clue: This Pulitzer-prize winning historian of The Imperial Presidency detailed the controversy of JFK needing voter support from McCarthy supporters in his book A Thousand Days.

question.leadin: Along with Wagner and Ellender, this man sponsored the National Housing Act of 1949.
question.text: Name this Senate Majority Leader known as "Mr. Republican," who more famously sponsored a labor relations act with Fred Hartley Jr.
question.clue: One profile in the book is of this man, nicknamed Mr. Republican, an Ohio senator who was the son of a president and who opposed the Nuremberg Trials as violating American ex post facto expectations.

swap.text: The Supreme Court ruled that states could require less than actual malice but at least negligence in a case named for Elmer Gertz and this man. The organization this man founded, the John Birch Society, was sued for claiming that Gertz was part of a communist conspiracy.
swap.clue: The essay claims the "mantle of McCarthy" has fallen on this man, the founder of the John Birch Society, and observes that this man's pamphlet attack Eisenhower as a Communist has over 100 pages of bibliography and endnotes.

question.text: Under the leadership of saleswoman Brownie Wise, this line of products was widely sold in the 1950s through a form of direct marketing called the "party plan," which involved women hosting social events for their friends and neighbors to try this line of products.

swap.text: In a 1971 meeting with Richard Nixon, this Ford executive convinced the president to oppose federal regulations that would make airbags mandatory on the grounds that "safety doesn't sell." This businessman wrote a best-selling autobiography in 1984 while he was CEO of Chrysler.
swap.clue: This CEO of Chrysler and author of a bestselling 1984 autobiography negotiated the concessions with UAW president Doug Fraser. He had previously overseen the development of the Mustang and Pinto during his time at Ford.
